label: rank
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{rank}  Let  $\gamma_0\triangleq 1$, and, for all $1\leq i\leq J$, let  the following be defined  in $\mathbb{F}_2[x]$: 
\begin{align*}&\gamma_i(x)\triangleq \gcd\{ \Delta_{\mathcal{J},\mathcal{L}}(x)\mid  |\mathcal{J}|=|\mathcal{L}|=i\},\\ 
&d_i(x) \triangleq \gcd (\gamma_i(x)/\gamma_{i-1}(x), x^N+1), \text{ where }\\ 
&\gcd(0/0,x^N+1)\triangleq \gcd(0,x^N+1)=x^N+1.\end{align*} Then,\begin{align*}
&\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F_2}(H)= 
J\cdot N -\sum_{i=1}^{J} \deg d_i(x).\\ 
\end{align*}

label: lemma:codeword:construction:1
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:codeword:construction:1}
Let $S \subseteq \{1, 2, \ldots, L\}$ be any subset of size $J+1$. Define the length $L$ vector $\mathbf{c}_S(x) = \left(c_{S,1}(x), c_{S,2}(x), \ldots, c_{S,L}(x)\right)$ over $R_N$ by $c_{S,i}(x) \triangleq \det H_{S \setminus \{i\}}(x)$ if $i \in S$, and $0$ otherwise, where $H_{S \setminus \{i\}}(x)$ is the $J \times J$ submatrix of $H(x)$ with columns indexed by $S \setminus \{i\}$. Then $\mathbf{c}_S(x)$ (as a column vector) lies in $\ker H(x)$.

label: minors-code
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{minors-code} Let $H_X (x)\in (R_N)^{J_X\times L}$. For a fixed  $\mathcal{S}\subset \{1, 2, \ldots, {L}\}$
of size ${J}_X $, form the column vectors  $\mathbf{c}_{\mathcal{S}\cup \{i\}}(x)$, for all $i\notin \mathcal{S}$. Define $H_Z(x) \in (R_N)^{J_Z\times L}$  with rows given by the vectors  
 $\mathbf{c}^\top_{\mathcal{S}\cup \{i\}}(x)$.  Then $H_XH_Z^\top=0$ and $C_X^\perp\subseteq C_Z$, so the length $NL$ code $\mathcal Q (C_X, C_Z)$ exists. If \[
\operatorname{rank}H_X+\operatorname{rank}H_Z<LN, 
\] then its dimension is positive. 
 
 In particular, if $L=J_X+1$, $H_Z=\begin{bmatrix} \Delta^\mathsf{T}_1& \Delta^\mathsf{T}_2&\ldots&\Delta^\mathsf{T}_L\end{bmatrix}$. If $L = J_X + 1$ and  $\gamma_{i,X}$ and  $d_{i,X}$ are defined as in Theorem~\ref{rank} for the matrix $H_X$, for all $1\leq i\leq J_X$,  then the dimension of  the  quantum code is
 \begin{equation}\label{dimension} K=\sum_{i=1}^{J} \deg d_{i,X}(x) + \deg  \gcd(\gamma_{J_X,X}, x^N+1).\end{equation}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
$\gamma_{J_X,X}$ is the gcd of all $J_X\times J_X$ minors $\Delta_i$ of $H_X$, and, therefore, it is the gcd of all the entries of the matrix $H_Z^T$, giving $d_{1,Z}(x)= \gcd(\gamma_{J_X,X}, x^N+1)$. 
  Then $ \operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F_2}(H_X)=  
J_X N -\sum_{i=1}^{J_X} \deg d_{i,X}(x) $ and $\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F_2}(H_Z)= \operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F_2}(H_Z^T)= N - \deg  \gcd(\gamma_{J_X,X}, x^N+1)$.
The dimension of $\mathcal Q$ now follows from \eqref{eq:cssdimension}.

label: thm:dimension
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:dimension}
Let \begin{equation} \label{eq:gcds} g_1(x)=\gcd(\Delta_1(x),\Delta_2(x),\Delta_3(x),x^N+1)\end{equation} and  \[
h=\gcd(gF,x^N+1).
\]
The dimension of $\mathcal Q$ is
\[
K=\deg g+\deg h+\deg g_1.
\]
In particular, for odd $N$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:factorK}K=\deg g+2\deg g_1
=3\deg g+2\deg f,
\end{equation}
where $f=g_1/g$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The Smith invariants of $H_X$ are $g$ and
$gF$, while the nonzero Smith invariant
of $H_Z$ is $g^2F$. 
Applying~\eqref{dimension} gives $K=\deg g+\deg h +\deg g_1$. 
For odd $N$, the polynomial $x^N+1$
is square-free. Since $g\mid x^N+1$,
\[
h=\gcd(gF,x^N+1)
=\gcd(g^2F,x^N+1)=g_1.
\]
The result follows.

title: Proof
body_md:
The row space of the circulant expansion of $z$ is $R_N z = \{rz \mid r \in R_N\}$, and $R_N qz \subseteq R_N z$. The map $r \mapsto rz$ from $R_N$ onto $R_N z$ has kernel $\{r \mid r\Delta_i \equiv 0 \pmod{x^N+1},\ i = 1,2,3\}$. For each $i$, $r\Delta_i \equiv 0$ if and only if $(x^N+1)/\gcd(\Delta_i, x^N+1)$ divides $r$, so the kernel is generated by
\[
\operatorname{lcm}_i \frac{x^N+1}{\gcd(\Delta_i, x^N+1)} = \frac{x^N+1}{g_1}.
\]
Hence $R_N z \cong \mathbb{F}_2[x]/\left((x^N+1)/g_1\right)$, with $z$ corresponding to $1$ and $qz$ to $q$. Thus $R_N qz = R_N z$ if and only if $q$ is a unit in this quotient, which is equivalent to \eqref{eq:q}.
